text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it actually does. Think of it like reorganizing a messy closet: you move things around, throw away old clutter, and label boxes, but the clothes themselves remain the same. In programming, this means renaming confusing variables, breaking long functions into smaller, focused pieces, and removing duplicate code. The main goal is to make the code easier to read and understand for humans, which reduces mistakes later. When you postpone refactoring, you build up “technical debt”—a kind of invisible interest you pay with slow development and bugs. By refactoring regularly, you keep your codebase clean, maintainable, and ready for future changes.
